title: Fresh Egg Pasta
subtitle: Basic fresh pasta dough
excerpt: Fresh pasta dough made from 00 flour and egg yolks. Silky, pliable, and entirely different from dried pasta. This is the base dough for tagliatelle, pappardelle, lasagne, and most filled pasta.

recipe.sourceNotes: Fresh egg pasta is one of the defining techniques of Northern Italian cooking, particularly in Emilia-Romagna, the Veneto, and Piedmont. The use of egg yolks for a richer, yellower dough is characteristic of Bolognese tradition.

recipeTools.notes: For rolling the dough. Can also be rolled by hand with a long pin.

content.text: Fresh egg pasta dough is made from 00 flour and whole eggs, with extra yolks for richness and colour. The dough needs to be well-kneaded to develop the gluten, then rested for at least 30 minutes before rolling, which makes it elastic and easy to work. It cooks in two to three minutes in boiling salted water.

Mound the flour on a clean work surface. Make a well in the centre. Break the eggs and yolks into the well. Add the oil and salt. Beat the eggs with a fork, gradually drawing in the flour from the inner wall. When the dough is too thick to use a fork, switch to your hands.

Knead the dough firmly for 8 to 10 minutes until smooth and elastic. Push the heel of your hand away from you, fold the dough back, turn a quarter, and repeat. The dough is ready when it springs back slowly when you press it with your finger.
Wrap the dough tightly in cling film or a beeswax wrap and leave to rest at room temperature for at least 30 minutes, or up to 2 hours.

Divide the dough into four portions. Keep the unused portions wrapped. Feed one portion through a pasta machine starting at the widest setting. Fold the sheet in thirds, turn it, and feed through again. Repeat two or three times until the sheet is smooth.

Continue rolling, reducing the setting by one notch each time, until you reach the desired thickness. For tagliatelle or pappardelle, setting 5 or 6 on most machines. For ravioli or lasagne, setting 6 or 7.
Cut and shape as required. To cook, boil in a large pot of well-salted water for 2 to 3 minutes until just tender.
